title: What If Venus Had Kept Its Oceans? It May Have Been Earthlike

scenes.text: What if Venus once looked like Earth? Climate models say it might have.
Today its surface sits at about 462 degrees Celsius, hot enough to melt lead.
NASA climate models suggest early Venus had a shallow ocean, with lowlands filled and highlands left as continents.
The simulations kept temperatures between about 20 and 50 degrees Celsius for roughly three billion years.
Then a huge release of gas, possibly from volcanic activity, set off a runaway greenhouse effect.
Venus may have been habitable for up to two billion years. Today it is the hottest planet in the solar system.
